notes: 1932 stamp is right: Wikipedia puts Zero's start as lobby boy and the main story in 1932. Rudeness line, the lobby boy speech ('completely invisible, yet always in sight', 'before the needs are needed'), the cheap cuts, 'Boy with Apple, stolen (by us)', 'Nobody move; everybody's under arrest' and 'nineteen consecutive seasons' all verbatim on Wikiquote. Checkpoint 19 is the prison (Shmoop symbol page). Tools in Mendl's pastries and the fall into the pastry van confirmed on Wikipedia. Cue prints on the phone only.

vibe.verdict: An in-room dining card from the Grand Budapest in 1932 with the Crossed Keys door hanger, Mendl's courtesan and Gustave's lines is very close to the film, though 'A lobby boy is completely invisible' prints twice.
missing: The guard slicing every pastry except Mendl's (the prison search)
'Keep your hands off my lobby boy!' (the train)
